purpose: Verify PPS, SOLO, PPLNS and PROP for Pearl using the shared accounting/payment implementations and real proof-enabled chain payouts.
automatedContracts: Distinct finder, proportional round and PPLNS window allocations from unequal assigned work; achieved jackpot luck does not change weights.
Reward-recipient fees allocated once; future shares excluded from older blocks; consecutive rounds/windows verified.
Concurrent/replayed maturity settlement cannot credit twice; pre-maturity orphan leaves balances unchanged; settled reorg holds payments.
PPS receipt, liability, remainder, balance and candidate intent commit atomically; failed candidate insertion and queue overflow leave no credit.
Candidate retirement cannot reverse accepted PPS liabilities; recorder-compatible serialized replay does not duplicate credit.
Both PPS arithmetic versions, durable administrator cutover, sub-unit remainder conservation and tampered liability rejection.
Oyster exact-output verification, whole-grain payments, residual balances, marker reconciliation and paid-ledger restart idempotency.
PPS requires local PostgreSQL and both payment switches; unsupported families/schemes still rejected.
PPLNS rejects zero, negative, null and string factors, including a later case-insensitive property alias.
limits: Live four-scheme mining used the already-certified BzMiner CPU profile over verified TLS on isolated proof-enabled regtest. Earlier mainnet-template and independent GPU-miner certification remains in the other Pearl reports.
PPS requires operator-funded spendable reserves; there is no automatic solvency or reserve-admission guarantee.
The final configuration guard was tested with all four pool startups and payout/restart verification; proof admission used the same reward-accounting implementation.
No skipped test is counted as live certification.
privacy: Public evidence omits host identities, addresses, credentials, operational paths, wallet keys and raw lab logs.
